= William de Glasgu (fl. 1394), Cleric =

== Biography ==
'''William de Glasgu''' (floruit 1394) was a Scottish cleric who appears in multiple Papal Petitions to Pope Benedict XIII, seeking ecclesiastical benefices in the diocese of Glasgow and the Abbey of Kilwinning.  

He is recorded in 1394 as "William de Glasgu, priest," requesting a benefice in the gift of the Abbot and Convent of Kilwinning and Kelso. These petitions place him firmly within the clerical network of southwest Scotland, specifically linked to the influential Tironensian Abbey of Kilwinning in Cunningham.

== Historical Context ==
Kilwinning Abbey was one of Scotland’s important Tironensian houses, founded by the de Morville lords of Cunningham in the late twelfth century. By the late 14th century, the abbey controlled extensive lands and numerous benefices, including churches in Ayrshire and connections to Paisley and Kelso. William’s application for a benefice indicates that he may have held or sought multiple church incomes (a practice common but increasingly regulated by papal dispensation).

No definitive surname beyond his locative “de Glasgu” appears in the papal rolls, and no alternate family name has been found in the Registrum of Kilwinning or Paisley. This strongly supports the interpretation that “de Glasgu” is a genuine surname or locative byname.

Not to be confused with Walter de Glasgu, In 1384 " Walter Wan, of the diocese of Glasgow," was authorised to hold a benefice in the gift of the abbot and convent of Kilwinning, "notwithstanding that he has the chapel of St. Mary in Glasgow<ref>https://electricscotland.com/history/glasgow/glasgow33.htm#:~:text=In%201384%20%22%20Walter%20Wan%2C%20of,has%20the%20chapel%20of%20St.</ref>


== Connections ==
* He is recorded alongside other clergy who held or sought Kilwinning benefices, including ties to the Abbey of Kelso.
* There is no evidence that he held the abbacy itself, but he may have served as a senior cleric or vicar in one of the dependent churches.

== Research Notes ==
At present, no additional contemporary records have been found clarifying whether William de Glasgu belonged to a known Glasgow family. No alternative surname or alias appears. His placement near Kilwinning and Paisley may connect him distantly to other early Glasgows active in church service during this period.

''Research ongoing. Further archival checks in the Paisley Registrum and papal calendars are advised.''
